data.body: Pushed as Gerrit 2062 (commit 9a0a16ef20), stacked on 2057. Held-out TDD: 9 tests authored, implementer saw only 3; the other 6 are divergence detectors. NOTE ON SHAPE: 8 of 9 passed before any implementation, because this consolidation has no new behaviour - so the held-out set is not 'edge cases the implementer could not see' but 'tests that catch an ERASED divergence'. The only genuinely RED requirement was the set-identity criterion. Both mutations killed by their exact held-out test: erasing the fc20 non-bug ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES narrowing killed test_the_non_bug_administrative_narrowing_is_preserved; flipping _recorded_replacement_target's on_subject_unreadable from 'continue' to 'stop' killed test_recorded_mode_continues_to_inbound_after_a_subject_reduce_failure. My FIRST attempt at that second mutation silently edited a DOCSTRING occurrence of the same literal and survived - worth recording, because a mutation that does not actually mutate reads exactly like a tautological test. Gates: lint rc=0, mypy 626 files clean, complexity new=0 increased=0 with two entries going stale (simpler), 72 pinning tests green with zero assertion edits, net -1 src lines, close_precheck.py 770 -> 726.
